newsitem.title: USA: Poll gives Clinton edge in Florida - report.
newsitem.headline: Poll gives Clinton edge in Florida - report.

text.p: President Clinton holds an eight percentage point lead over Republican challenger Bob Dole in Florida, according to a new poll published by the Miami Herald Tuesday.

According to the independent Florida Voter Poll, 47 percent of the state's voters favoured Clinton, versus 39 percent for Dole. Eight percent backed Reform Party candidate Ross Perot and 6 percent were undecided.
The poll was conducted by the nonprofit Forman Centre for Political Studies in Fort Lauderdale. It questioned 576 likely voters between Oct. 19 and Oct. 26, with a margin of error of 4.2 percent.

The poll showed the race for the state's 25 electoral votes, the fourth highest total in the country, had tightened from the last Florida Voter Poll six weeks ago, which showed Clinton leading Dole by 50 percent to 38 percent, with 8 percent for Perot and 4 percent undecided.

The poll showed Dole's strongest backing in Florida among "hardcore Republicans" and among white men, who favoured him by 45 percent to 39 percent, the newspaper said. Among women, Clinton led 55 percent to 34 percent.

The poll also found that fewer than half of the state's voters favoured a proposal to impose a $0.01 per pound tax on Florida sugar to pay for cleanup of the Everglades ecosystem. Support for the tax dropped from 60 percent a month ago to a current 47 percent.
